title: Shell setup tests must stub commands and pass fixtures without POSIX symlinks or argv, to run on Windows Git Bash
answers: mlflow agent setup tests fail on Windows
setup_sh unit tests break under Git Bash
how do I fake curl or sed in test_setup_sh_unit tests
why does json_escape test fail on Windows with MSYS
body:
Symptom: The `mlflow agent setup` shell unit tests fail on Windows (Git Bash) even though the setup script works there.
Root cause: tests/agent/test_setup_sh_unit.py:test_json_experiment_strings_fallback_handles_compact_response and test_local_server_always_prints_mlflow_command built fake commands as symlinks or executable files in tmp_path and passed that directory as PATH. test_json_escape passed a backslash-and-quote value as a shell argument, which MSYS argument conversion rewrites.
Fix pattern: Put the fixture value inside the shell snippet (raw r""" string assigned to a variable) instead of passing it as $1. Replace PATH-dir stubs with shell functions defined in the snippet (e.g. `curl() { :; }`). When the real binary is still needed, capture it first with `sed_bin=$(command -v sed)` and then clear PATH and define `sed() { "$sed_bin" "$@"; }`.
Constraints: The production setup script is not changed by this pattern; it applies only to the test file. Function stubs only intercept bare-name calls made by the script. Path results should be compared with `Path(result.stdout.strip()) == expected`, not string equality, because Windows separators differ.
applies: Tests in tests/agent/test_setup_sh_unit.py that run setup.sh functions through run_shell; not for tests that must exercise real executables.
says: Agent setup unit test suite fails when running on Windows developer machines.
Setup script verification tests break on Windows when using Git Bash terminal.
The setup test suite reports errors caused by Windows file path separator differences.
Make automated setup script tests run reliably across both Linux and Windows environments.
Setup command tests fail on Windows because quotes and backslashes are modified.
search: In tests/agent/test_setup_sh_unit.py, shell setup unit tests running setup.sh via run_shell must define in-snippet shell function stubs and raw string fixtures instead of PATH symlinks or argv arguments to support Windows Git Bash. Passing fixtures as $1 triggers MSYS argument conversion bugs on backslashes and quotes, while PATH-dir stubs fail on Windows. When real binaries like sed are needed, capture them with command -v before clearing PATH, and compare paths using Path equality rather than string equality to handle Windows separators. This rule applies strictly to unit tests in test_setup_sh_unit.py intercepting bare-name calls, not to the production setup.sh script or tests requiring real executables.
